column3: The Hebrew refers to the animals with plural “them”; BSB uses singular “it.”
The Hebrew joins the brother’s distance and not knowing him with “and”; BSB gives alternative conditions with “or.”
The Hebrew repeats “and thus you shall do” three times; BSB states the action once for the three categories.
The Hebrew refers to the fallen animals with plural “them”; BSB uses singular “it.”
The Hebrew first names a man’s equipment or articles and then a woman’s garment; BSB uses “clothing” in both clauses.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the falling root in “the falling one falls”; BSB says “someone falls.”
The Hebrew uses the root for becoming holy or consecrated; BSB says the harvest will be “defiled.”
The Hebrew says the animals are together without an explicit word “yoked”; BSB supplies “yoked.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the corners “wings” and repeats the covering root for the garment and covering oneself; BSB says “corners of the cloak you wear.”
The Hebrew says to take a woman and come in to her; BSB expresses this as marrying her and having relations with her.
The Hebrew says “I did not find virginity for her”; BSB recasts this as “I discovered she was not a virgin.”
The Hebrew separately says to take and bring out the evidence and repeats “the young woman”; BSB says “bring” and uses “her” for the second reference.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the man did not find virginity and explicitly repeats “my daughter”; BSB says he discovered she was not a virgin and uses “her” in the father’s reply.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives “a hundred silver” without an explicit unit and says he cannot “send her away”; BSB supplies “shekels” and says “divorce her.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew actively says “they shall bring out” the young woman; BSB uses the passive “she shall be brought.”
The Hebrew repeats “the woman” in describing the man lying with her; BSB uses “her.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats that the man lay with her; BSB refers to this as “has done this.”
The Hebrew repeats “the young woman” and speaks of killing a “soul”; BSB uses “she” for the second reference and “murders him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives “fifty silver” without an explicit unit and says he cannot “send her away”; BSB supplies “shekels” and says “divorce her.”
The Hebrew says not to uncover the father’s “wing” or garment edge; BSB expresses this as not dishonoring his father’s “marriage bed.”
